findings.title: Two-zone continuation pays 288 SSE per gradient instead of the fused 97
findings.claim: _optimize_space_only.move_starts runs L-BFGS-B with a callable jac that evaluates float(objective(x)) as f0 plus a scalar fun. Each gradient costs 96 batch rows + 2 scalar horizons = 288 SSE, against 97 for the fused value-and-gradient the main loop uses. Across a 6-cell two-zone no-DHW grid, fusing removes 13.5-31.1% of total solve SSE, or 13.5-29.2% after dropping the largest cell. The flat-price cell removes 29.2%, so the cost does not depend on prices. The iterate path is unchanged: main gradient counts are identical in both arms.

findings.title: _gil_yield's sleep(0) does not bound the loop starvation of an in-process solve
findings.claim: On the #511 in-process fallback, the solve runs on an executor thread. During a two-zone solve the event-loop heartbeat's max gap is 87-124 ms and the starvation share is 0.70-0.89. The idle null control in the same session shows 14-21 ms and 0.08-0.17. Removing _gil_yield barely changes the gap, while a real 0.1 ms sleep cuts it to about 30 ms. So the per-evaluation sleep(0) does not act as a GIL handoff.

findings.phenomenon_property: A GIL yield implemented as time.sleep(0) inside the solver thread does not hand the GIL to a waiting event-loop thread.
